text: The Noetic Learning math contest is a national biannual problem-solving competition designed for elementary and middle school students in grades 2 through 8. It was founded in 2007 by Li Kelty and is based in Overland Park, Kansas. The contest aims to foster students' interest in mathematics and enhance their problem-solving abilities. It is held twice a year, in the fall and spring, and consists of a 45-minute timed test with 20 math problems. The competition has grown significantly, with participants from schools across the United States. In Spring 2023, more than 35,000 students nationwide took part. Students can earn various awards and recognition based on their performance, and school teams are also eligible for specific awards.
